items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Code Quality Enterprise Policy empowers organizations with control over the availability of Code Quality at the enterprise level. By separating Code Quality from Code Security policy management, enterprises can confidently enable Code Quality functionality for their teams without risk of incurring Code Security-related costs.

Expected Outcome

With the new Code Quality enterprise policy, administrators can provide developers access to code quality insights while maintaining strict control over security settings and spend. This separation helps organizations manage adoption based on their needs and ensures compliance with internal governance and budgeting requirements.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality: Enterprise Policy [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Users can now assign code scanning alerts—individually or within a security campaign—to an agentic version of Autofix that autonomously creates pull requests to fix the problem. Unlike the current Autofix, this agentic version uses tool calling and advanced agent behaviors to iteratively test, validate, and refine fixes before presenting them to developers.

This release covers the initial public preview, focused on campaigns and individual alerts. A separate GA release will follow.

Expected Outcome

  • Increased rate of security alert remediation across customer organizations
  • Higher Autofix acceptance rates compared to current non-agentic version
  • Reduced time from alert creation to merged fix
  • Decreased manual effort spent on security debt reduction initiatives
items.title: Agentic autofix generation for code scanning alerts [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

When Sentry pinpoints the root cause of an error, you shouldn’t have to stop and switch tools to get it fixed. This feature lets you launch the Copilot coding agent straight from Sentry Root Cause Analysis (Seer), automatically carrying over the right context so you can go from insight to action in a single click.

Expected Outcome

Faster fixes with less friction. Instead of copying stack traces, hunting down the right files, and re-explaining the problem in GitHub, you can generate a strong first pass at the code change immediately and move straight into review. The result: shorter time-to-fix for Sentry issues, smoother on-call and triage workflows, and more time spent shipping improvements, not stitching together context across tools.
items.title: Launch Copilot coding agent from Sentry Root Cause Analysis

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Many engineering teams live in Jira to plan, triage, and assign work, yet they have to leave Jira to actually kick off implementation with Copilot coding agent. This release brings Copilot coding agent into Jira, so you can assign our coding agent to a Jira work item (from the assignee dropdown or via @mention) and let it start working with the right task context.

Expected Outcome

Less friction between planning and shipping. Teams can delegate well scoped coding tasks to Copilot directly from Jira, and still keep code review and merging in GitHub. The result can lead to a smoother workflow for Jira centric teams and faster progress from “assigned” to “PR ready for review”.
items.title: GitHub Copilot for Jira: Pubic Preview

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Copilot intelligently routes requests to the best model for a developer's specific task, allowing them to benefit from improved service reliability and less rate limiting, all without the cognitive load of model selection. Auto continues to align with model policies and provides discounted model rates for paid plans, providing cost optimization alongside performance.

Expected Outcome

Developers get faster, more relevant results without needing to choose models manually, increasing productivity and consistency across use cases. Organizations benefit from simplified adoption, improved experience at scale, and clearer value realization through smart, cost-aware routing.
items.title: A more intelligent Copilot auto model selection, optimizing for your task

items.content_html:
Value Prop

On March 1, 2026 the $0.002 per-minute Actions cloud platform charge will begin applying to self-hosted runner usage in private repositories.

This will not impact Actions usage in public repositories or GitHub Enterprise Server customers.

Expected Outcome

This aligns pricing to match consumption patterns, ensuring consistent service quality across hosting modalities as usage grows. This will result in significant improvements to our self-hosted offering, including the following releases over the coming year:

GitHub Scale Set Client

This new client provides enterprises with a lightweight Go SDK to build custom autoscaling solutions without the complexity of Kubernetes or reliance on ARC. It integrates seamlessly with existing infrastructure—containers, virtual machines, cloud instances, or bare metal—while managing job queuing, secure configuration, and intelligent scaling logic. Customers gain a supported path to implement flexible autoscaling, reduce setup friction, and extend GitHub Actions beyond workflows to scenarios such as self-hosted Dependabot and custom automation agents.

Multi-Label Support

We are reintroducing multi-label functionality for both GitHub-hosted larger runners and self-hosted runners, including those managed by Actions Runner Controller (ARC) and the new Scale Set Client.

Actions Runner Controller 0.14.0

This release introduces major quality-of-life improvements, including refined Helm charts for easier Docker configuration, enhanced logging, updated metrics, and formalized versioning requirements. It also announces the deprecation of legacy ARC, providing a clear migration path to a more reliable and maintainable architecture. Customers benefit from simplified setup, improved observability, and confidence in long-term support, reducing operational friction and improving scalability.

Actions Data Stream

Actions Data Stream will deliver a real-time, authoritative feed of GitHub Actions workflow and job event data, including metadata such as action versions. This capability enhances observability and troubleshooting by enabling organizations to integrate event data into monitoring and analytics systems for compliance and operational insights. By providing structured, high-fidelity data at scale, it eliminates reliance on manual log parsing and empowers teams to proactively manage reliability and performance.
items.title: GitHub Actions new pricing - Self-hosted runner price increase

items.content_html:
Value Prop

On January 1, 2026, GitHub will reduce the price of GitHub-hosted runners by up to 39%. The free usage minute quotas will remain the same.

This reduction is driven by a price reduction of base rates on all runners, paired with a new $0.002 per-minute GitHub Actions cloud platform charge. For GitHub-hosted runners, the new Actions cloud platform charge is already included in the reduced meter price.

Usage of standard GitHub-hosted runners in public repositories will remain free.

Expected Outcome

This price reduction makes high-performance compute more accessible for both high-volume CI workloads and the agent jobs that rely on fast, secure execution environments.

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Multi-label support in Actions Runner Controller (ARC) gives enterprises the flexibility to manage complex workflows without duplicating infrastructure. Instead of maintaining separate scale sets for each configuration, customers can assign multiple labels. For example a single scale set could have labels that represent attributes for operating system, hardware, compliance, and network configuration. This capability simplifies runner management, reduces operational overhead, and ensures jobs land on the right compute resources with minimal effort.

Expected Outcome

Customers gain a streamlined approach to autoscaling and job routing, improving resource utilization and reducing idle capacity. This results in lower infrastructure costs, faster execution, and better alignment with compliance and performance requirements, delivering an efficient and scalable self-hosted runner experience.
items.title: Multi-Label Support for Actions Runner Controller (ARC)

items.content_html:
Value Prop

ARC 0.14.0 delivers a more streamlined and reliable experience for managing self-hosted runners at scale. With refined Helm charts for easier Docker configuration, improved logging for faster troubleshooting, updated metrics aligned with platform availability initiatives, and formalized versioning requirements, this release reduces operational complexity and enhances observability. It also introduces a clear migration path by announcing legacy ARC deprecation, ensuring customers can transition to a more robust and maintainable architecture.

Expected Outcome

Customers benefit from simplified configuration, better visibility into runner health, and improved reliability across their environments. These enhancements reduce friction during setup and maintenance, minimize downtime through clearer metrics and logging, and provide confidence in long-term support through structured versioning. By moving away from legacy ARC, organizations gain a modern foundation that supports scalability and future innovation, creating a more predictable and efficient experience for platform teams.
items.title: Actions Runner Controller Release 0.14.0

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Actions Data Stream is a real-time streaming endpoint that provides authoritative, high-fidelity data about workflows, jobs, and associated metadata across an organization.

Expected Outcome

It enables enterprises to capture actionable insights such as job states, runner labels, triggering events, and action versions, while offering extensibility for future high-volume data like network logs. Designed for integration with GitHub’s ecosystem, the data stream transforms operations by allowing teams to automate dashboards, anomaly detection, and governance.
items.title: GitHub Actions Data stream

items.content_html:
Value Prop

The Scale Set Client gives enterprises a flexible way to build custom autoscaling solutions without the complexity of Kubernetes or reliance on ARC. It provides a lightweight Go SDK with core primitives for managing runner scale sets, allowing customers to integrate with their own infrastructure such as containers, virtual machines, cloud instances, or bare metal. The client handles job queuing, secure just-in-time configuration, and intelligent scaling decisions while customers retain full control over provisioning logic. This capability extends beyond GitHub Actions workflows and can also support self-hosted Dependabot, Copilot Coding Agent, and any workload that leverages GitHub Actions self-hosted compute.

Expected Outcome

Customers gain a clear, supported path to implement autoscaling that fits their unique operational models, delivering flexibility without the complexity of Kubernetes or reliance on webhooks. This improves the overall experience by reducing setup friction, enabling faster scaling decisions, and allowing teams to integrate seamlessly with their existing infrastructure. Organizations can extend GitHub Actions beyond traditional workflows to power automation scenarios like self-hosted Dependabot or custom agents, creating a more unified and efficient CI/CD environment.
items.title: Scale Set Client

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Actions will address the long-standing community ask to provide parallel steps in GitHub Actions

Expected Outcome

TBD - we will work with the community to understand how we can best implement parallel steps
items.title: Parallel Steps in GitHub Actions

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Today Actions often fails to render the page if a workflow has over 300 jobs, and is then hard to navigate. We will implement lazy loading and filtering to solve this

Expected Outcome

Customers with very large numbers of jobs should still be able to use and navigate within the Actions UI
items.title: Support over 300 jobs & filtering in the Actions UI

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Expressions in GitHub Actions currently do not support any sort of logical operations to select a value based on a conditional. This feature will give users more power to create complex expressions that meet their specific needs and include that logic in the config instead of having to store it somewhere else.

Expected Outcome

We will introduce a new case function in GitHub Actions that will allow if/else if/else logic in GitHub Actions expressions.
items.title: Support new conditional operator in GitHub actions

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Customers that trigger a workflow using the workflow dispatch endpoint would like the response to include some metadata that would allow them to map the request to a workflow run. Currently, only an HTTP response code is returned.

Expected Outcome

Developers who need to identify which runs originated from a workflow_dispatch event, can do so without the need of extensive API polling or building their own custom solution.
items.title: Return runID from workflow_dispatch

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Customers have expressed the need to support more than just UTC for scheduling jobs in GitHub Actions, Especially when the schedule is only supposed to run on certain days of the week this gets very confusing with UTC

Expected Outcome

We will provide timezone support for cron/scheduled jobs in GitHub Actions
items.title: Actions supports timezones for scheduled workflows

items.content_html:
Value Prop

The MCP registry and allowlist controls for GitHub Copilot in JetBrains, Eclipse, and Xcode provide administrators and developers with a secure and streamlined way to manage access to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. By enabling curated discovery and installation of MCP servers from a central registry, and enforcing allowlist policies, organizations gain better oversight and control, improving security and simplifying setup across popular IDEs.

Expected Outcome

Organizations can expect easier setup and management of MCP server access for Copilot users in JetBrains, Eclipse, and Xcode IDEs. Developers will have a simple, reliable experience finding and installing approved MCP servers, while admins can enforce policies to restrict usage to only trusted servers. This reduces security risks, increases compliance, and saves time for both IT and engineering teams.
items.title: MCP registry and allowlist controls for Copilot in JetBrains, Eclipse, and Xcode [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

The new 1 vCPU / 5 GB RAM standard hosted runners for GitHub Actions provide a lightweight, cost-effective option for automation tasks, issue operations, and short-running jobs. By running workflows inside containers instead of full virtual machines, these runners make it easier and more efficient for teams to execute simple automation at scale while saving on compute resources.

Expected Outcome

Teams using these lightweight runners can expect faster startup times and reduced resource costs for smaller automation jobs. This enables organizations to run more jobs in parallel, optimize their CI/CD pipelines, and focus heavier compute resources where needed, all while lowering costs for lightweight tasks.
items.title: Actions: New 1 vCPU standard hosted runner [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Enterprise Cloud now supports unaffiliated users for all enterprises, enabling organizations to manage Copilot Business licensing and enterprise team membership independent of organization affiliation. Enterprise owners can invite users directly to the enterprise account and assign Copilot licenses without requiring organizational membership, providing greater flexibility in managing user access and licensing. This separation of enterprise membership from organization membership allows enterprises to centralize all user management under one account, whether users need access to GitHub Enterprise, Copilot, or both—streamlining administration and reducing complexity.

Expected Outcome

Organizations can expect more flexible and granular control over user management and Copilot licensing at the enterprise level. Enterprise administrators will be able to invite and license users for Copilot without the overhead of organization membership, making it easier to onboard contractors, external collaborators, or Copilot-only users. However, this change requires an important update to offboarding processes: users removed from all organizations will now remain as unaffiliated users in the enterprise, requiring explicit removal from the enterprise itself. Teams should audit their offboarding automation to ensure users are fully removed when needed, preventing unintended license consumption or access.
items.title: Unaffiliated users for GitHub Enterprise Cloud [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub secret scanning now surfaces extended metadata for leaked secrets, helping security and development teams understand ownership and impact at a glance. Beyond verifying whether a secret is active, secret scanning now displays details like the secret owner's name and email, creation and expiry dates, and organizational context for supported providers such as OpenAI, Slack, Stripe, and many others. This additional context transforms secret alerts from simple detections into actionable intelligence, enabling teams to quickly determine who owns a leaked secret, what it can access, and where it originates.

Expected Outcome

Organizations can expect faster triage and more effective remediation of leaked secrets. With ownership and impact information readily available, security teams can prioritize alerts more accurately, contact the right stakeholders immediately, and assess the scope of potential exposure without time-consuming manual lookups. Development teams benefit from clearer context that helps them understand the severity of each alert and take informed action. As GitHub continues to add support for additional secret types on a rolling basis, teams will gain increasingly comprehensive visibility into their secret exposure across their entire development stack.
items.title: Extended metadata checks for secret scanning [Preview]
